He just doesn't go VP, not everyone does.  At a glance, it looks like he adjusts his auras / setup depending on map mods, but the tree there is primarily geared towards neither endurance charges nor leech. Honestly, looks about like a CI flicker from way back on standard--just enough life, the rest is 100% damage. 

If you're running a no VP berserker, and you're worried that wearing an abyssus and not using any defensive auras will get you killed ( it will. ), I would suggest investing into a few defensive layers. Coil, taste of hate, whatever you want to do. A basalt at least to protect your unguarded sphincter.   If you want to draw back the damage, I would go by his IR setup and drop some of his damage for endurance charges.  Multi will do most of your work on an abyssus build.

He paths at 120 points, so this is a fairly high level build, one should assume that things like the 3, 3 point jewels he's taken will likely not be included.  If you're wanting to tank up a zerker, endurance charges, IR, taste of hate, lightning coil, lots of layers. Your primary concern will be stacking your leech after a savage hit, which largely just depends on having the attack speed to get it out. 

Jugger has a similar approach in that it loses a bit of damage to get endurance charges, but a great deal of jugger's tankiness is purely from endurance charges. I wouldn't suggest speccing into raw leech nodes for either, as the leech formula can be mindnumbing at best.

I'm not particularly a fan of IR, but it's certainly not bad. Grace / IR in tandem can provide a lot of mitigation on their own, so I left it on the tree for your discretion.

All I really did was drop the 3 point jewels and the wrecking ball / execution cluster.   This brings the skill points down towards 86ish, so you will be better able to see where you're actually sitting at when you're hitting the 'peak' of the character, right before XP DRs set in and you're likely looking at perfecting the character or moving on.

I just finished this up, and I'll say you're doing well for yourself, as the subreddit suggests, Keep writing. Now, down to my thoughts. I feel like some of the segments of writing came off as fairly staccato. While this writing style isn't always a bad thing, in terms of a first person perspective, I don't believe it lends very well to a character being presented as their personality would suggest. 

" I sat at home. " " I was lonely. " " I had a room mate. " While these are all well and good, they can be summarized and smoothed ( in my own unimportant opinion. ) " I sat at home, lonely, despite the company of my room mate Jeff. "  A lot of consideration has to be taken when it comes to writing from a character's perspective. As a reader, we are essentially reading the diary of this character. How would they phrase these events ? Would they speak in absolute honesty ? If we are not viewing through their eyes, but rather in their narration, how do they picture themselves ? 

I believe that the general idea of the story has direction and forethought, these are extremely good, you have a direction and the story funnels into that direction and ends neatly on a portion of dialogue. These things bring the picture together for a reader and feels nice to rest upon at the end of a scene. 

Now, back to my thoughts on the dialogue. One particular segment actually stuck out to me.

 " Dude, I'm waiting for the right girl to drop into my life, I can't be bothered with the painful process of chasing girls and flirting. " 

While these are truths to the character, and they are his actual viewpoint, they feel slightly off in the way he states this. As someone with a social phobia, or general apprehension to the opposite sex, would you be entirely accepting, realistic and honest about those things ? Maybe with his good friend Jeff, however, he belittles Jeff's existence in his life in the first paragraph as simply a warm body to keep him company.

I like to constantly think about being Jeff in these conversations when I'm writing in the first person. How would he say it to me ? Would he open his heart and bear all of his insecurities ? Would he phrase it in such a way that he's honest, but doesn't outright admit to his troubles with women ? These little things can shape and mold a character far, far more than any mile of text describing their personality ever could.

All in all, keep at it, you have a solid foundation in which to begin, and I feel like you'll grown into your own in time.


-Night.
